scenes.name: El oficio: del air guitar al dios del metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El músico de heavy sale del público: es el fan que toca la guitarra de aire en el concierto de UFO de 1979 y quiere estar donde está Michael Schenker. No hay escuela ni beca: hace falta talento musical y dramático (actuar la emoción por trescientas veces), un cuerpo joven y atlético (correr y pesas en la gira, el pelo largo como signo de autenticidad) y aprender a vivir en un grupo que no es ni familia ni oficina, con sus «problemas de ego» por la rivalidad entre cantante y guitarrista. El heavy es el estilo más caro de montar y casi no hay clubes donde empezar; el código exige temas propios y autenticidad. Firmar con un sello convierte a la banda en una empresa del capitalismo tardío frente a un oligopolio. El ciclo es componer, grabar (paciencia; el primer disco de Black Sabbath se hizo en doce horas, Spreading the Disease de Anthrax en cinco meses) y girar (aguante: esperar, esperar). La recompensa no es el dinero sino el carisma del chamán que alcanza el éxtasis dionisíaco ante miles de personas; el precio, «quemarse o apagarse», porque nadie que viva lo bastante puede cumplir el código.

podcast.title: Investigation for Black Ice (September 27, 1986)
podcast.body: Following Cliff Burton's fatal bus accident, James Hetfield searched the highway extensively for the reported black ice but couldn't find any. This contributed to rumors surrounding the cause of the accident, though an investigation later ruled it a routine winter traffic accident. "James Headfield went up and down the highway looking for this black ice but he couldn't find any."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: CBL & Orion Tribute to Cliff Burton
podcast.body: Above his right elbow, James has the letters "CBL," which are the initials of former Metallica bassist Cliff Burton. Under his inner left arm, there are musical notes that transcribe the song "Orion," a track written by Cliff Burton, serving as a tribute to him after his death in a 1986 tour bus accident. "Just above his right elbow are the letters CBL. Then there were some musical notes under his inner left arm. That's a transcription of the song Orion, which is in tribute to former Metallica bass player Cliff Burton, who died in a tour bus accident in 1986."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive and Intricate Tattoos
podcast.body: James Hetfield of Metallica has at least 26 intricate tattoos, each with a story. "The guy from Metallica has at least 26 tats, not a lot compared to others, but they are very, very intricate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Flaming Playing Cards (Birth Year & Pyro Accident)
podcast.body: On his left shoulder, Hetfield has flaming playing cards (an ace, a nine, a six, and a three) representing 1963, his birth year. The flames themselves reference a 1992 incident in Montreal where he caught fire due to ill-timed pyro during a concert. "On his left shoulder are some flaming playing cards, an ace followed by a nine, a six, and a three. So 1963, the year he was born. So 1963, 1963, the year he was born. The flames are in reference to the time he literally caught fire because of some ill-time pyro during a 1992 show in Montreal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Injuries Requiring Substitute
podcast.body: James Hetfield of Metallica has twice needed his guitar tech, John Marshall, to fill in for him due to injuries. One incident involved a broken arm from skateboarding, and another was a result of being badly "synched" by ill-timed pyrotechnics. "Once after Hetfield broke his arm while skateboarding and another time when he was badly synched by some ill-time pyro."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: M81 (Metallica Formation Year)
podcast.body: On his right hand, Hetfield has "M81," with "M" standing for Metallica and "81" representing 1981, the year the band was formed. "On his right hand, you can see M81. That's M for Metallica and 81 for the year in which the band was formed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Matthew 6:13 (Addiction Reference)
podcast.body: On his left wrist, Hetfield has "Matthew 6:13" tattooed, referencing the biblical verse "lead us not into temptation," which is most likely connected to his personal struggles with addiction. "And still with the Bible, he has Matthew 613 tattooed on his left wrist. That's lead us not into temptation, which most likely has something to do with his addiction issues."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: St. Michael and St. James Illustration
podcast.body: Further up his arm, there is an illustration depicting a fight between St. Michael and St. James, reflecting Hetfield's long-standing interest in religious stories. "And going up a little further, there's an illustration of a fight between St. Michael and St. James. James has always had a thing for religious stories."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cliff Burton's Death (1986)
xref.body: Former Metallica bassist Cliff Burton died in a tour bus accident in 1986. His initials (CBL) and a transcription of his song "Orion" are tattooed on James Hetfield as a tribute. "That's a transcription of the song Orion, which is in tribute to former Metallica bass player Cliff Burton, who died in a tour bus accident in 1986."

xref.title: Filled in for James Hetfield Twice
xref.body: John Marshall has twice stepped in to perform for James Hetfield of Metallica when Hetfield was unable to play. One instance occurred after Hetfield broke his arm skateboarding, and another when he was injured by ill-timed pyrotechnics. "He filled in twice for Hetfield. Once after Hetfield broke his arm while skateboarding and another time when he was badly synched by some ill-time pyro."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Guitar Tech for James Hetfield
xref.body: John Marshall is the dedicated guitar tech for James Hetfield of Metallica. He previously played guitar for the band Metal Church before taking on this role. "John Marshall is the guitar tech for Metallica's James Hetfield."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: James Hetfield's Stance on Military Use
xref.body: James Hetfield, Metallica's frontman, is on record as supporting the troops' use of Metallica's music in war zones. He stated that he takes it as an honor, believing their song could help quell an attack like 9/11, despite the assumption that the band should be offended their music is used to break people down psychologically. "James Hetfield is on record as supporting the troops use of Metallica's music in war zones."
